currentIdentity.ruleTitleVerbatim: RULE 3.989. SWORN STATEMENT; PETITION; AND ORDER TO EXPUNGE OR SEAL FORMS
currentIdentity.subdivisionHeadingVerbatim: (a) Sworn Statement in Support of Petition.
currentIdentity.issuerBasis: The Court promulgates the Rules of Criminal Procedure under article V, section 2(a) of the Florida Constitution. The instrument is a court-promulgated form printed inside the rule, not an agency form.
currentIdentity.roleDetail: A sworn instrument filed in support of the petition to expunge or seal. It is not the petition — the petition is subdivision (d) — and it is not an order. The repository's expectedDocumentRole of affidavit remains functionally correct after the retitle: a sworn statement subscribed before an officer authorized to administer an oath is an affidavit in substance. The role does not change; the document's name does.
currentIdentity.participantFacingBasis: The instrument is written in the first person by the petitioner: 'I, .....(name of defendant/petitioner)....., am the defendant/petitioner in the above-styled cause and I do hereby swear or affirm that:', followed by six numbered averments. The signature line is captioned Petitioner.
currentIdentity.attestation: Sworn to and subscribed before a notary public or other person authorized to administer an oath
currentIdentity.attestationVerbatim: Sworn to and subscribed before me on .....(date)...... / NOTARY PUBLIC, or other person authorized to administer an oath / Printed, typed, or stamped commissioned name of Notary Public / Personally known .......... or produced identification ........... / Type of identification produced .................... / My commission expires:
currentIdentity.attestationNote: The rule says notary public or other person authorized to administer an oath. It does not say deputy clerk; the phrase deputy clerk appears nowhere in Rule 3.989. A deputy clerk is such an authorized person under Florida law, so the Florida memo's component note is substantively right and verbally looser than the rule. Recorded as a precision point, not as an error, and no memo text was changed.
mandatoryBasis: § 943.0585(3), Fla. Stat.: 'Each petition to expunge a criminal history record must be accompanied by: (a) A valid certificate of eligibility issued by the department. (b) The petitioner's sworn statement that he or she: 1. Satisfies the eligibility requirements for expunction in subsection (1). 2. Is eligible for expunction to the best of his or her knowledge and does not have any other petition to seal or expunge a criminal history record pending before any court.'

§ 943.059(3), Fla. Stat., mirrors it for sealing: 'Each petition to a court to seal a criminal history record is complete only when accompanied by: (a) A valid certificate of eligibility issued by the department pursuant to this section. (b) The petitioner's sworn statement that the petitioner: ...'
Both statutes make a knowingly false sworn statement a third-degree felony, which is a further indication that the sworn instrument is an operative filing rather than an optional attachment.
Rule 3.989(a) supplies the prescribed form of that statutorily required sworn statement.
currentIdentity.mandatoryConsequence: The repository's requirement value of required is correct and must not be relaxed. A petition filed without the sworn statement is incomplete on the face of the sealing statute.
currentIdentity.scopeDetail: The form is prescribed statewide by the Supreme Court of Florida and applies in every circuit. The instrument itself is captioned for a circuit-court filing: 'In the Circuit Court of the ..... Judicial Circuit, in and for ..... County, Florida', with Case No. and Division. Statewide prescription and circuit-court venue are both true and are not in tension; the Florida memo's track geography scope of circuit records the venue, not a limit on the form's authority.
currentIdentity.scopeCaution: Statewide prescription does not license substituting a circuit or county packet reproduction. See doNotSubstitute.

misboundComponent.finding: This component's own recorded legal basis is § 943.0583, Fla. Stat., the human-trafficking expunction statute. The same 2019 opinion that retitled Rule 3.989 moved the human-trafficking forms out of it into Rule 3.9895. The instrument this component needs is Rule 3.9895(b), 'Sworn Statement in Support of Petition; Human Trafficking Victim.', which is a subdivision of a different rule with a different caption implementing a different statute. Rule 3.989(a)'s averments do not fit: its paragraph 5 recites no prior expunction under §§ 943.0585 or 943.059, and its paragraph 6 addresses expunction petitions under the general route. Neither speaks to trafficking-victim status under § 787.06. The trafficking instrument's own paragraph 2 is the substantive averment of victim status under § 787.06, and Rule 3.989(a) has no equivalent.
misboundComponent.wasCoherentBefore2019: Yes, and that is the diagnosis. Pre-2019 Rule 3.989(f) was 'Affidavit in Support of Petition; Human Trafficking Victim', printed caption 'AFFIDAVIT/HUMAN TRAFFICKING VICTIM'. The binding was defensible against the superseded rule and became wrong on 2019-12-19. It is not a random error; it is the same unapplied amendment that left the title stale.
